recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If explicit court-order terminology is desired beyond the existing third-party, personal-representative, and substitute-decision-maker language, open a new tracker for work-group consideration.
issue_request: FHIR-23705 requested Consent introduction language allowing legal consent on another's behalf, including third-party and/or court-ordered consent; the Published/Persuasive resolution approved general wording for choices or agreements made on the healthcare consumer's behalf by a third party.
initial_application: No FHIR-23705-tagged source commit was found. Git history shows bbe7cd28ea added the third-party/on-behalf wording to Consent narrative definitions and spreadsheet source soon after the Jira decision; later Consent refactors preserved the wording and moved it into current notes and StructureDefinition surfaces.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini. Current combined-branch sources include the resolved wording in the StructureDefinition description/root definition, a personal representative in the Consent scope introduction, third-party grantor wording in the privacy consent model, and Substitute Decision Maker language in the supporting narrative. Focused Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting later decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys that Consent can represent choices made on behalf of the healthcare consumer by a third party, and adding separate court-order prose would exceed the accepted resolution without fixing a semantic gap.
